intro: Chang'e 5 landed in Mons Rümker on December 1, 2020 — China's first lunar sample-return mission and the first lunar sample return by any nation since Luna 24 (1976), 44 years earlier. Returned 1,731 g of samples from young volcanic terrain (~2 billion years old, compared to ~3.5 Ga Apollo samples), proving that lunar volcanism continued far later than previously known.

images.caption: Chang'e 5 stack — four-element vehicle: lander/ascender (surface), orbiter (lunar rendezvous), reentry capsule (Earth return).
Drill + scoop subsystem — collected samples from both the surface and 1+ m depth.
Long March 5 launches Chang'e 5 — China's most ambitious lunar mission to that point, fully automated 23-day round trip.
Chang'e 5 on the surface near Mons Rümker — 19 hours of operations before ascent stage liftoff.
